locator.section: 8 / Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Random or hidden rearrangements; hydrogen exchange in an ion-molecule complex)

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.7, first step (arrow labelled 'rH'). The n-hexanal molecular ion, n-ionized at the carbonyl oxygen (drawn O+.), transfers its gamma-H to oxygen through a 6-membered TS, giving the distonic radical cation: odd electron now on the gamma carbon, oxygen protonated (H-O+=CH). Book draws 2 arc(s): the large arc from the gamma C-H toward oxygen and the fishhook of the O+. odd electron are drawn; move <3> (the second electron of the breaking gamma C-H bond remaining on the gamma carbon as the new radical) is an implicit homolysis hook -- the resulting radical dot is drawn on the product but not as its own arc. Electron balance: the forming O-H bond receives 2 e- (moves 1,2); the breaking gamma C-H bond routes both its electrons (move 2 into O-H, move 3 onto the gamma carbon). This is the common entry step for both the high-energy (Eq 8.7 row 1) and low-energy (Eq 8.7 rows 2-3) channels.
